The test image shows a soybean stem/root system with:
- Dead fibrous roots at the top
- Very dark brown/black lesion in the upper stem (near root collar)
- Tan to yellow-brown intermediate zone
- Healthy green stem at the bottom

This suggests a stem/root rot disease. Top candidates: Phytophthora, Rhizoctonia, Pythium_damping_off, Fusarium.

Now I'll view one reference from each of my top candidates.

**Analysis:**

- Test image: A soybean plant (likely seedling/young plant) pulled from soil. Shows dead/withered fibrous roots at top, very dark brown-to-black lesion extending from the root collar area down the stem, transitioning to tan/yellow, then healthy green at the base.

- **Phytophthora** reference: Showed brown stem discoloration at plant bases with wilted leaves — somewhat matching the dark stem decay pattern, but the reference was a field shot.
- **Rhizoctonia** reference: Showed reddish-brown, sunken dry canker localized at soil line — less extensive than the test image's dark lesion.
- **Pythium_damping_off** reference: Showed very early seedling collapse at soil surface — different presentation.
- **Fusarium** reference: Showed pale/whitish stem discoloration — different color from the dark/black lesion in the test image.

**Reasoning:** The test image shows very dark brown-to-black discoloration extending from the root collar area upward along the stem, with a gradual transition zone to tan/yellow, then green healthy tissue below. This matches Phytophthora best: "dark chocolate-brown stem discoloration extending from below the soil line upward" with root rot and degradation. Rhizoctonia is localized at the soil line as a dry canker; Pythium shows water-soaked soft rot in very young seedlings; Fusarium shows paler discoloration. The extent and darkness of the lesion here best fits Phytophthora.
